name: Front lid, composite panel
description: 993 front lid reproduced in composite from the original steel panel. Bolted skin part, with no structural function and no anti-intrusion bar, retained as the first lightweight body pilot.

classification.intended_use: Closes the front compartment; the part carries no load, but its retention is a safety matter at high speed

provenance.record_license: MIT for the record, geometry not yet produced

sources.title: Paul Stephens Autoart - 993R, body weight reduction
sources.notes: Confirms that the original lid is steel and that a Porsche Motorsport aluminum version weighs 8 kg.

sources.title: Specialist press - Gunther Werks, carbon-bodied 993
sources.notes: Precedent of a 993 body made entirely of carbon prepreg, with the steel body shell kept and reinforced.

sources.title: Federleichte Elfer - mass table, 993 exterior parts
sources.notes: Original front lid 14.0 kg; lightweight versions claimed at 5.0 kg in GFK polyester, 4.9 kg in GFK epoxy and 4.1 kg in carbon epoxy.

material.grade: fiber and resin to be determined; glass, carbon or hybrid

post_processing: fitting of the hinge and latch interfaces

titanium.galvanic_isolation: not applicable, composite part; provide isolation for the metal inserts

known_limits: Class functional and not non_critical: the panel carries nothing, but a lid that comes loose at high speed is a safety event. The hinge and latch interfaces are therefore the critical dimensions, not the skin.

Original mass claimed at 14.0 kg by a German tuner, consistent with the 8 kg Porsche Motorsport aluminum lid. Claimed carbon epoxy target: 4.1 kg, a gain of about 9.9 kg. These masses are claimed, not weighed by this project: weighing the donor panel remains step zero.
Porsche part number transcribed from catalogue Kat 017: 993 511 010 01, and 993 511 010 31 for the Carrera RS. Variant and model year of the donor vehicle remain to be confirmed.
The mold must be taken from a sound, undeformed original panel: a crash-damaged lid would give a wrong part.
Fiber, resin, layup and core not defined. A poorly designed glass laminate can be heavier than the original steel.
Fire behavior, under-hood temperature resistance and UV aging not evaluated.
Regulatory compliance not studied: a change of body material may require an inspection depending on the country of registration.
